label: Affinity 66
description: The original 66-grouping representation-weight scheme (draft-v0.1.2 Pipeline v2 content wave), authored without a population max/min factor target. Kept unchanged for back-compat; see the 'balanced' scheme for a max-factor <=7 alternative (amendment A3.1).

groupings.name: Vienna–Eastern Austria
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton; Vienna's national weight and distinct metropolitan/Pannonian character justify standalone representation, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

groupings.name: Austria outside Vienna (Styria–Carinthia–Tyrol–Salzburg–Upper Austria–Vorarlberg)
groupings.rationale: Non-capital Austria combined into one representation grouping; each Land keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity (Vorarlberg's special_status dual Swiss/Tyrolean orientation among them).

groupings.name: German-speaking Switzerland (Zürich–Basel–Bern–Ostschweiz)
groupings.rationale: All German-speaking Swiss cantons combined into one representation-weight bloc (Bern's federal-capital role stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased here); distinct from the French- and Italian-speaking language regions.

groupings.name: Romandie (French-speaking Switzerland)
groupings.rationale: Distinct national language community (French); not merged across the Röstigraben into German-speaking groupings.

groupings.name: Ticino (Italian-speaking Switzerland)
groupings.rationale: Distinct national language community (Italian); geographically separated by the Alps from the rest of Switzerland.

groupings.name: Alpine & Western European Microstates
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: five fully sovereign European microstates (populations ~800-90,000), each far too small individually for 40-70 representation weight. Clustered across borders per the explicit microstate convention; each remains its own cultural unit and sovereign state.

groupings.name: Alemannic Southwest (Baden-Württemberg)
groupings.rationale: Mirrors the real Land Baden-Württemberg (one Landtag, Stuttgart, since 1952). Baden/Württemberg split at the cultural-unit layer per Alemannic/Swabian dialect and pre-1952 statehood, reunited here for representation.

groupings.name: Bavaria (Franconia–Swabia–Altbayern)
groupings.rationale: Mirrors the real Land Bayern (one Bayerischer Landtag, Munich). Franconia/Bavarian Swabia/Munich-Altbayern split at the cultural-unit layer per distinct dialect/historic identity, reunited here for representation.

groupings.name: Western Germany (Hesse–Rhineland-Palatinate–Saarland–NRW)
groupings.rationale: Western German Länder along the Rhine-Main/Rhine-Ruhr-Saar corridor, geographically contiguous; each Land/historic region (Hesse, Rhineland, Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland) keeps its own cultural-unit identity, combined here for representation weight since five separate western blocs would push the count past the 40-70 target.

groupings.name: Hanseatic North Germany (Hamburg–Bremen–Schleswig-Holstein–Lower Saxony)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous North Sea/Low-German (Plattdüütsch) coastal Länder sharing Hanseatic trading heritage; grouped for representation weight while each city-state/Land keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Neue Bundesländer / Eastern Germany (Saxony–Thuringia–Saxony-Anhalt–Berlin–Brandenburg–Mecklenburg-Vorpommern)
groupings.rationale: The standard German term 'Neue Bundesländer' for the former-East-Germany Länder plus Berlin, sharing post-1990 reunification/GDR administrative history; Berlin's capital-city weight stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

groupings.name: Flanders
groupings.rationale: Distinct Dutch-speaking community/Region with its own Parliament; large enough to stand alone.

groupings.name: Francophone Benelux (Wallonia–Brussels–Luxembourg)
groupings.rationale: Wallonia and Brussels share French-language civic space with neighbouring Luxembourg; Luxembourg is a small sovereign state clustering cross-border per convention, while each unit keeps its own identity/parliament.

groupings.name: Randstad (Amsterdam–Rotterdam)
groupings.rationale: The two Randstad conurbation units, contiguous and functionally integrated, kept distinct as cultural units (Amsterdam/Utrecht vs Rotterdam/Zeeland) but combined here for representation weight.

groupings.name: Nederland buiten de Randstad (Noord–Oost–Zuid)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous Dutch provinces outside the Randstad conurbation; Zuid-Nederland's distinct Catholic-south Brabantian/Limburgish identity preserved as its own cultural unit, combined here for representation weight.

groupings.name: Île-de-France (Paris)
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton; population and national weight justify standalone representation.

groupings.name: Nord-Ouest (Hauts-de-France–Normandy–Brittany–Pays de la Loire)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous northern/western France sharing a Channel-and-Atlantic-coast orientation; Brittany's distinct Breton/Celtic identity preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

groupings.name: Sud-Ouest (Aquitaine–Midi-Pyrénées)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous southwestern France, Gascon/Occitan cultural sphere.

groupings.name: Sud-Est (Languedoc-Roussillon–PACA–Corsica–Rhône-Alpes–Auvergne–Burgundy-Franche-Comté)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous southeastern quadrant of France; Corsica's distinct identity and Auvergne/Burgundy-Franche-Comté's split from Rhône-Alpes at the cultural-unit layer (Clermont-Ferrand vs Lyon vs Dijon/Besançon) preserved as separate cultural units, reunited here for representation weight since a six-bloc French layer would overshoot the 40-70 target.

groupings.name: Grand Est (Alsace–Lorraine–Champagne)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous northeastern France; Alsace's distinct Alemannic-German-influenced identity preserved as its own cultural unit.

groupings.name: Noroeste (Galicia–Asturias–Cantabria)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous Atlantic Celtic-tinged northern Spain, each region too small alone for the target; Galicia's own language preserved as its own cultural unit.

groupings.name: Noreste (Basque Country–La Rioja–Aragon)
groupings.rationale: Ebro-valley/Pyrenean neighbours of the Basque Country; Basque Country's distinct language/identity and own parliament preserved as its own cultural unit, grouped only for representation weight.

groupings.name: Madrid
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton.

groupings.name: Centro y Sur (Castile-León–Castile-La Mancha–Extremadura–Andalusia–Murcia–Ceuta y Melilla)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous inland-Meseta and southern Spain (Castile-La Mancha borders Andalusia/Murcia directly); each region and the special_status North-African exclaves keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity, combined here for representation weight.

groupings.name: Catalan-Speaking Mediterranean Arc (Catalonia–Valencia–Balearics)
groupings.rationale: Catalan/Valencian linguistic continuum along the Mediterranean coast (former Crown of Aragon); Catalonia and Valencia each keep distinct cultural-unit identity and own institutions.

groupings.name: Canary Islands
groupings.rationale: Atlantic archipelago, geographically and culturally distinct from mainland Spain; large enough to stand alone.

groupings.name: Gibraltar
groupings.rationale: British Overseas Territory, special_status; sovereignty distinct from Spain, kept a standalone singleton rather than merged into Spanish groupings.

groupings.name: Mainland Portugal (Lisboa–Alentejo–Algarve–Porto–Centro)
groupings.rationale: All mainland-Portugal cultural units combined into one representation grouping; each region (including Algarve's distinct tourism-region identity) keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Atlantic Autonomous Regions (Azores–Madeira)
groupings.rationale: Portugal's two Atlantic autonomous-region archipelagos, each with own regional parliament, clustered here as remote island territories for representation weight.

groupings.name: Nord-Ovest (Piedmont–Liguria–Lombardy)
groupings.rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Nord-Ovest'.

groupings.name: Nord-Est (Veneto–Friuli–Trentino–South Tyrol–Emilia-Romagna)
groupings.rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Nord-Est', which spans Triveneto plus Emilia-Romagna; South Tyrol's special linguistic-autonomy status preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

groupings.name: Centro (Tuscany–Umbria–Marche–Lazio)
groupings.rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Centro', which includes Lazio/Rome alongside Tuscany, Umbria and Marche; Rome's national capital weight is a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

groupings.name: Mezzogiorno Continentale (Campania–Puglia–Abruzzo–Basilicata–Calabria)
groupings.rationale: Mainland-southern Italy, corresponding to the pre-unification mainland provinces of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies (roughly ISTAT 'Sud'); each region keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity (Neapolitan, Apulian, Calabrian etc.).

groupings.name: Isole (Sicily–Sardinia)
groupings.rationale: Official ISTAT/Eurostat NUTS-1 macro-region 'Isole'; Sicily and Sardinia each keep their own distinct island cultural-unit identity (Sicilian vs Sardinian, the latter its own Romance language) and special-statute autonomy, combined here only for representation weight.

groupings.name: Poland (Mazovia–Łódź–Małopolska–Eastern Poland–Silesia–Lower Silesia–Wielkopolska–Pomerania)
groupings.rationale: All eight Polish cultural units combined into one representation grouping; central/southeastern Poland (around Warsaw/Kraków) and western/northern Poland (former Prussian-partition sphere plus Baltic coast) each keep their own distinct regional cultural-unit identity (Silesian, Kashubian-Pomeranian etc.).

groupings.name: Czechia (Bohemia–Moravia–Czech Silesia)
groupings.rationale: All three Czech cultural units combined into one representation grouping, satisfying the 'Czech units -> 1-2 groupings' mandate at the low end; Bohemia and Moravia-Silesia each keep their own historic identity as cultural units.

groupings.name: Slovakia (Bratislava–East)
groupings.rationale: Both Slovak cultural units combined into a single representation grouping; each keeps its own identity (western Bratislava core vs eastern Košice/Prešov, with its Rusyn/Hungarian minority character).

groupings.name: Hungary (Budapest–West–Balaton–East/Debrecen)
groupings.rationale: All four Hungarian cultural units combined into one representation grouping, satisfying the mandated 'four Hungarian units -> 1-2 groupings' at the low end; Budapest's capital-city weight stays a cultural-unit-level distinction, not erased by the grouping.

groupings.name: Slovenia–Croatia
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small contiguous, EU-member, formerly-Yugoslav Adriatic states, clustered for representation weight (analogous to the Baltic States/South Caucasus clusters); each remains fully sovereign, Slovenia as its own cultural unit and Croatia's continental/Adriatic-coast regions each keeping their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Western Balkans (Bosnia–Serbia–Montenegro–North Macedonia–Albania–Kosovo)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY/POLICY-BASED CLUSTER matching the EU's own 'Western Balkans' policy grouping (the six EU-enlargement candidates/entities of the region). Every member (Bosnia's three parliament-mandated entities, Serbia's Belgrade-core and autonomous Vojvodina, and the four small sovereign/de-facto states) keeps full cultural-unit identity and, where mandated, its own parliament; this grouping is purely a representation-weight bloc for otherwise very small/fragmented states, not a claim of shared identity.

groupings.name: Romania (Transylvania–Banat–Székely Land–Wallachia–Moldavia)
groupings.rationale: All five Romanian cultural units combined into one representation grouping; the historic Transylvanian bloc (including the Hungarian-Székely autonomous cultural unit) and the Old-Kingdom Wallachia-Moldavia core each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Bulgaria (Sofia–Plovdiv–North Danube–Varna)
groupings.rationale: All four Bulgarian cultural units combined into one representation grouping; western/southern Bulgaria and the northern Danubian/Black-Sea regions each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Athens–Attica
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton; roughly a third of national population, kept separate as with other large-country capitals (Paris, Madrid, Vienna).

groupings.name: Greece outside Attica (Macedonia–Thrace–Peloponnese–Crete–Aegean)
groupings.rationale: Non-capital Greece combined into one representation grouping; Macedonia (Thessaloniki) and Thrace (Komotini/Alexandroupoli) each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity per the mandated split.

groupings.name: Mediterranean Microstates (Cyprus–Malta)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small sovereign Mediterranean island EU member states, clustered across (non-contiguous) borders for representation weight per the microstate convention; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit (Cyprus's de-facto Greek/Turkish-Cypriot split stays flagged separately at the unit layer).

groupings.name: Manner-Suomi (Helsinki–Turku–Tampere–Oulu–Lapland–Lakeland)
groupings.rationale: Mainland Finland combined into one representation grouping (southern coastal belt plus interior/northern Finland including Sámi Lapland); each region keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Åland
groupings.rationale: Swedish-speaking autonomous archipelago with its own parliament; kept a standalone singleton given its distinct autonomy status.

groupings.name: Stockholm (Östra Sverige)
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

groupings.name: Sweden outside Stockholm (Gothenburg–Malmö–Gotland–Norrland)
groupings.rationale: Non-capital Sweden combined into one representation grouping; southern Sweden (including formerly-Danish Scania) and Norrland each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Denmark (Copenhagen-Zealand–Jutland-Funen)
groupings.rationale: Mainland Denmark's two cultural units combined into one representation grouping.

groupings.name: Oslo Region (Eastern-Southern Norway)
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton, kept separate as with other large-country capitals.

groupings.name: Norway outside Oslo (Vestlandet–Trøndelag–Nord-Norge)
groupings.rationale: Non-capital Norway combined into one representation grouping; the western fjord coast, Trøndelag and the Sámi north each keep their own distinct cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: North Atlantic (Iceland–Faroe Islands–Greenland)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: Iceland (sovereign) plus the Faroe Islands and Greenland (self-governing Danish Realm territories), clustered as small/remote North Atlantic territories for representation weight; each keeps its own sovereignty/autonomy status flagged at the unit layer.

groupings.name: Baltic States (Estonia–Latvia–Lithuania)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: three small sovereign Baltic states, each too small individually for 40-70 representation weight, clustered per the explicit Baltic convention; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit.

groupings.name: London
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton.

groupings.name: Southern & Midlands England (Sussex–Wessex–Solent–Exeter/Plymouth–Cornwall–Birmingham–East Midlands–Cambridge)
groupings.rationale: England outside London and the North, combined into one representation grouping since England alone would otherwise take an outsized share of the 40-70 budget; Cornwall's distinct Cornish identity preserved as its own cultural unit within the bloc.

groupings.name: Northern England (Manchester–Liverpool–Lancashire–Yorkshire–Newcastle)
groupings.rationale: Consolidated 'Northern Powerhouse' belt (Lancashire/Yorkshire/North East), each metro area keeping its own cultural-unit identity; combined for representation weight since England alone would otherwise take an outsized share of the 40-70 budget.

groupings.name: Wales–Scotland
groupings.rationale: The two devolved Great Britain nations outside England (own Senedd/Holyrood), combined into one representation grouping; Wales and Scotland (Central Belt and Highlands) each keep their own distinct national/cultural-unit identity, not merged with any England grouping.

groupings.name: Northern Ireland
groupings.rationale: Kept a standalone singleton per the mandated distinct-unit-in-every-view treatment; not merged with Great Britain groupings or with the Republic of Ireland grouping given its distinct UK sovereignty status.

groupings.name: Ireland (Dublin–Cork–Galway)
groupings.rationale: Republic of Ireland's three cultural units combined into one representation grouping.

groupings.name: Crown Dependencies (Guernsey–Jersey–Isle of Man)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: three British Crown Dependencies (not part of the UK proper), each far too small individually, clustered per the explicit convention; each remains its own cultural unit.

groupings.name: Western & Central Ukraine (Lviv-Galicia–Volhynia–Zakarpattia–Kyiv–Hetmanate–Podillia)
groupings.rationale: Contiguous western and central Ukraine (historically Austro-Hungarian/Polish-influenced west, capital-region center); each region keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Southern & Eastern Ukraine (Odesa–Crimea–Kharkiv–Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia–Donetsk–Luhansk)
groupings.rationale: Black Sea coast, Crimea and the eastern/Donbas oblasts (conflict_flags apply at the unit layer, unaffected by this representation-weight grouping); each region keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Moldova
groupings.rationale: Sovereign state, single cultural unit; no adjacent small-state cluster fits without stretching geographic/cultural logic, kept standalone.

groupings.name: South Caucasus (Georgia–Armenia)
groupings.rationale: SOVEREIGNTY-BASED CLUSTER: two small contiguous sovereign South Caucasus states, clustered for representation weight; each remains its own sovereign cultural unit.

groupings.name: East Thrace
groupings.rationale: Isolated European sliver of Turkey (Turkey otherwise out of scope); kept a standalone, flagged singleton.

label: Balanced (max-factor <=7)
description: Representation-grouping scheme built to keep the population max/min factor across non-exempt groupings at or under 7 (European-Parliament-style degressive-proportionality target), per amendment A3.1. Special_status cultural units (microstates, city-states, disputed/exclave territories, Piedmont) sit outside the factor calculation as their own dashed singleton or micro-cluster groupings (see factor_exempt). Every other default-visible cultural unit belongs to exactly one of the remaining groupings, built by splitting the affinity-66 scheme's oversized lumps (Poland, Germany-West, France Sud-Est/Nord-Ouest, UK South-Midlands, Ukraine West-Center/South-East, Romania) along existing cultural-unit lines, and by merging undersized units upward by affinity (e.g. Aland into mainland Finland, Ticino into a Swiss bloc, Malta into Sicily-Sardinia, the Azores/Madeira into Porto-Norte).

groupings.name: Gibraltar
groupings.rationale: British Overseas Territory, disputed sovereignty with Spain; kept as its own dashed representation singleton rather than folded into a Spanish or UK grouping.

groupings.name: Alpine Microstates
groupings.rationale: Sovereign European microstates (Liechtenstein, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino, Vatican City) clustered as one dashed representation grouping outside the population-factor calculation, matching their special_status.

groupings.name: Crown Dependencies
groupings.rationale: Self-governing Crown Dependencies (Guernsey, Jersey, Isle of Man) grouped as one dashed special-status cluster, outside the UK cultural-unit groupings and outside the factor calculation.

groupings.name: Vorarlberg
groupings.rationale: Special_status dual Swiss/Tyrolean-oriented Land; kept as its own dashed singleton rather than merged into the Austria-outside-Vienna bloc, consistent with its special_status flag.

groupings.name: Brussels
groupings.rationale: Capital enclave / EU district with special_status; kept as its own dashed singleton distinct from Flanders and Wallonia.

groupings.name: Cyprus
groupings.rationale: De-facto divided island (Greek Cypriot south / Turkish Cypriot north administration); special_status singleton, outside the factor calculation regardless of its ~0.92M population.

groupings.name: Berlin
groupings.rationale: City-state special_status Land; kept as its own dashed singleton apart from Brandenburg/the eastern Länder bloc.

groupings.name: Bremen
groupings.rationale: City-state special_status Land; kept as its own dashed singleton apart from the Lower Saxony/Schleswig-Holstein bloc.

groupings.name: Hamburg
groupings.rationale: City-state special_status Land; kept as its own dashed singleton apart from the Lower Saxony/Schleswig-Holstein bloc.

groupings.name: Ceuta & Melilla
groupings.rationale: Discontiguous North African exclaves with disputed sovereignty; special_status singleton, kept out of the Andalusia-anchored grouping and out of the factor calculation.

groupings.name: Piedmont
groupings.rationale: Marked special_status per explicit instruction (Alpine Occitan/Franco-Provençal valleys plus Savoy-core history, 'special zone like Monaco'); kept as its own dashed singleton and excluded from the factor calculation even though its ~4.4M population would otherwise sit comfortably inside the band.

groupings.name: East Thrace
groupings.rationale: Out-of-scope-state landmass inclusion (Turkey excluded as a whole; shown only for European-landmass completeness); dashed special_status singleton, outside the factor calculation.

groupings.name: Vienna–Eastern Austria
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton; Vienna's metropolitan and Pannonian weight justifies standalone representation like other large-country capitals (Madrid, Budapest, Paris).

groupings.name: Austria outside Vienna (and Vorarlberg)
groupings.rationale: The non-capital, non-Vorarlberg Austrian Länder combined into one balanced-scheme grouping (4.64M); individually none of Styria, Carinthia, Tyrol, Salzburg or Upper Austria clears the ~2.6M representation floor set by the largest single-unit grouping (London), so they stay merged even though each keeps its own distinct cultural-unit identity. Styria and Carinthia sit together inside this grouping by explicit affinity (their pairing is separately endorsed); Carinthia's contested southward alignment is offered as an alternative to the Slovenia-Croatia grouping.

groupings.name: German-speaking Switzerland & Ticino
groupings.rationale: Zürich, Basel, Bern-Mittelland and Schaffhausen (German-speaking) plus Ticino (Italian-speaking) combined for population balance: Ticino alone (0.35M) falls far under the representation floor and has no land neighbor cluster of its own size, so it is paired here as one of Ticino's two plausible representation homes (see alternatives).

groupings.name: Romandie & Alpine Central-Eastern Switzerland
groupings.rationale: French-speaking Romandie (1.7M) also falls under the representation floor alone; paired with Central-Eastern Switzerland's Alpine cantons (Graubünden and neighbors, which border both Romandie and Ticino) as a population-balancing grouping and Ticino's alternative home.

groupings.name: Baden-Württemberg
groupings.rationale: Historic Baden and Württemberg, split as cultural units on the 1806-1952 statehood/dialect boundary, recombined here as one representation grouping (11.07M) matching today's federal state; comfortably inside the balanced-scheme band without further splitting.

groupings.name: Bavaria (Franconia–Swabia–Altbayern)
groupings.rationale: All of non-exempt Bavaria combined (12.98M); under the effective ceiling set by London's 18.3M single-unit grouping, so no further split is required to satisfy the ≤7 factor even though each sub-region keeps its own cultural-unit identity.

groupings.name: Hesse–Rhineland-Palatinate–Saarland
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old affinity-scheme's 29.17M 'Germany West' lump along cultural-unit lines. Saarland (0.98M) is far under the representation floor alone and is merged upward with its immediate neighbor Rhineland-Palatinate by affinity (shared Prussian Rhine Province/French-border history); Hesse joins to keep the piece comfortably inside the band (11.33M). Saarland's own 1947-1957 quasi-French Saar Protectorate history is offered as an alternative alignment with French-East (Alsace-Lorraine).

groupings.name: Rhineland
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 29.17M 'Germany West' lump; Rhineland alone (9.56M) clears the representation floor comfortably as its own grouping, keeping the populous Rhine-Ruhr corridor from being merged with unrelated territory.

groupings.name: Westphalia
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 29.17M 'Germany West' lump; Westphalia alone (8.28M) clears the representation floor comfortably as its own grouping.

groupings.name: Lower Saxony–Schleswig-Holstein
groupings.rationale: Hamburg and Bremen (both special_status city-states) are pulled out to their own exempt singletons; the remaining Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony stay merged as one grouping (10.94M), just inside the balanced-scheme band.

groupings.name: Saxony–Thuringia–Saxony-Anhalt–Brandenburg–Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
groupings.rationale: Berlin (special_status city-state) pulled out to its own exempt singleton; the remaining five eastern Länder stay combined as one grouping (12.5M) since that is comfortably under the effective ceiling and none would individually clear the representation floor.

groupings.name: Flanders
groupings.rationale: Belgium's Dutch-speaking Community/Region stands alone as one grouping (6.89M), unchanged from the affinity scheme; Brussels (special_status) is exempted separately.

groupings.name: Wallonia–Luxembourg
groupings.rationale: French-speaking Wallonia combined with the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; Luxembourg alone (0.66M) is far under the representation floor and has no other francophone neighbor to merge with, so this pairing (matching the existing affinity-scheme structure) is kept.

groupings.name: Randstad (Amsterdam–Rotterdam)
groupings.rationale: The Netherlands' core conurbation belt combined as one grouping (10.73M); comfortably under the effective ceiling, no split needed.

groupings.name: Netherlands outside the Randstad
groupings.rationale: Groningen, the Deventer/Overijssel/Achterhoek hub and South Brabant-Limburg combined as one grouping (7.05M); comfortably under the effective ceiling, no split needed.

groupings.name: Île-de-France (Paris)
groupings.rationale: Paris and its region form a single, unsplittable cultural unit at 12.3M; kept as its own mega-grouping like Vienna, Madrid and London — well inside the ≤7 factor set by London's 18.3M.

groupings.name: Hauts-de-France–Normandy
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 19.1M 'France Nord-Ouest' lump along cultural-unit lines; the two northern coastal/Channel regions combined (9.29M) clear the representation floor comfortably.

groupings.name: Brittany–Pays de la Loire
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 19.1M 'France Nord-Ouest' lump; Brittany and Pays de la Loire combined (9.81M) clear the representation floor comfortably.

groupings.name: Aquitaine–Midi-Pyrénées
groupings.rationale: Southwest France combined as one grouping (9.22M), unchanged from the affinity scheme; comfortably under the effective ceiling.

groupings.name: Languedoc-Roussillon–Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur–Corsica
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 19.27M 'France Sud-Est' lump along cultural-unit lines; the Mediterranean-coast regions plus Corsica combined (8.34M) clear the representation floor comfortably.

groupings.name: Rhône-Alpes–Auvergne–Burgundy-Franche-Comté
groupings.rationale: Split out of the old 19.27M 'France Sud-Est' lump; the Lyon-anchored bloc combined with Auvergne and Burgundy-Franche-Comté (10.93M) clears the representation floor comfortably (both were already split out as separate cultural units from Lyon/Aquitaine per the content-wave mandate).

groupings.name: Alsace–Lorraine–Champagne
groupings.rationale: France's eastern border regions combined as one grouping (5.54M); none of Alsace (1.9M), Lorraine (2.33M) or Champagne (1.31M) clears the representation floor alone. Alsace's contested German-Baden orientation and Lorraine's contested German-Rhineland/Saarland orientation are both offered as alternatives.

groupings.name: Galicia–Asturias–Cantabria
groupings.rationale: Spain's Atlantic-coast northwest combined as one grouping (4.29M), unchanged from the affinity scheme; Asturias (1.0M) and Cantabria (0.58M) do not clear the floor alone.

groupings.name: Basque Country–La Rioja–Aragon
groupings.rationale: Spain's northeast interior combined as one grouping (4.55M), unchanged from the affinity scheme; La Rioja (0.32M) and Aragon (1.34M) do not clear the floor alone.

groupings.name: Madrid
groupings.rationale: Capital-region singleton (6.75M), unchanged from the affinity scheme.

groupings.name: Castile–Extremadura–Andalusia–Murcia–Canary Islands
groupings.rationale: Split target from the old affinity scheme's centro-sur bloc kept merged rather than fragmented: at 17.86M it stays comfortably under the effective ceiling. The Canary Islands (2.24M) are added here because, standing alone, they fall under the representation floor and have no adjacent land neighbor; Andalusia's historic Atlantic trade link to the Canaries (colonization routed via Cádiz/Seville) gives the merge an affinity basis, offered against the alternative of grouping with Portugal's Atlantic islands instead.

groupings.name: Catalonia–Valencia–Balearic Islands
groupings.rationale: Spain's Catalan-speaking Mediterranean arc combined as one grouping (14.18M), unchanged from the affinity scheme; comfortably under the effective ceiling.

groupings.name: Lisbon–Alentejo–Algarve–Centro
groupings.rationale: Southern and central mainland Portugal combined as one grouping (6.64M); Alentejo (0.7M), Algarve (0.47M) and Centro (2.2M) do not clear the representation floor alone.

label: Balanced — within states
description: Representation-grouping scheme built with the same population max/min-factor method as 'balanced' (amendment A3.1), but with an added hard constraint: no grouping's member cultural units may span more than one country (amendment A4.1). This is stricter than 'balanced', which merges some undersized units across a state border by affinity (e.g. Moldova into a Romanian grouping, Iceland/Greenland/Faroe into a Norwegian one) to hit the <=7 target. Honest trade-off: small sovereign states with no larger domestic partner to merge with (Iceland, Malta, Cyprus, Slovenia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Luxembourg), plus Greenland and the Faroe Islands (non-sovereign constituent countries of the Kingdom of Denmark, but similarly unable to merge upward at this dataset's country-code granularity), cannot be folded into any grouping without crossing a border, so they sit outside the factor calculation as their own 'sovereign_floor' entries -- structurally unable to merge upward, not merely special_status. The two pre-existing special_status clusters that already crossed borders in the balanced scheme (Alpine Microstates, Crown Dependencies) stay unchanged as factor_exempt (consistent with 'specials stay as marked'); no new cross-border factor_exempt cluster was introduced -- Greenland/Faroe went to sovereign_floor instead, so the border-crossing factor_exempt set remains exactly the two the task named. The resulting 'computed_factor' (population max/min across the remaining non-exempt, non-sovereign_floor groupings) is reported honestly rather than forced to <=7 -- comparing it against affinity-66's and balanced's computed_factor IS the argument for or against allowing cross-border representation merging.
